title: Sneakers sports shoes to fashion icons
titleChinese: 运动鞋：从体育用品到时尚的象征
paragraphs: Many of us wear trainers, or sneakers as they are called in American English. They might not seem like anything special, but these items of footwear have become an obsession for some people. Get ready to meet the sneakerheads.

From their beginnings as practical footwear for athletes, trainers or sneakers have become big business. They are now a massive part of the global fashion industry, and the sneaker market could be worth $120bn by 2026. Trainers started to gain cultural cachet in the 1970s due to the popularity of basketball and football in US and UK youth culture, says fashion gallery curator Ligaya Salazar. Celebrity endorsements from the likes of Run DMC and Michael Jordan boosted the market through the 1980s and 90s. Brendan Dunne, host of a podcast dedicated to sneakers, describes how, as they became cooler and more expensive, sneakers became status signifiers.

While most trainers are made for the mass market, limited-edition pairs are made to appeal to those who are looking for something special. Sneakerheads are those who collect rare trainers, sometimes paying thousands of dollars for a pair. Dunne compares it to art collecting, pointing out that they have been sold by major auction houses and are seen by some as an investment.

Trainer manufacturers have seen this market for rare sneakers as a good business opportunity and have teamed up with celebrities to produce limited edition pairs. This feeds into the resale market for this footwear. Some sneakerheads spend hours camping outside shops to get their hands on the most desirable limited editions which they can then flip for a huge profit.
So, an item that started as an everyday functional object for people playing sports can now also be a high-fashion item worth thousands of dollars.

vocabulary.entry: **curator** /kjʊəˈreɪtə(r)/ n. 策展人，馆长（书面语）

vocabulary.example: The footballer's endorsement of the brand helped increase its popularity.

vocabulary.entry: **dedicated to** /ˈdedɪkeɪtɪd tu/ phr. 致力于，专门用于
vocabulary.example: The museum is dedicated to the history of the city.
vocabulary.translation: 这座博物馆专门展示这座城市的历史。

vocabulary.entry: **status signifier** /ˈsteɪtəs ˈsɪɡnɪfaɪə(r)/ n. 地位象征（书面语）
vocabulary.example: In some cultures, a luxury car is a major status signifier.
vocabulary.translation: 在某些文化中，豪车是一个重要的地位象征。

vocabulary.entry: **mass market** /ˌmæs ˈmɑːkɪt/ n. 大众市场
vocabulary.example: The product was redesigned to appeal to the mass market.
vocabulary.translation: 该产品经过重新设计以吸引大众市场。

vocabulary.example: The watch is a limited-edition model, with only 500 made.
vocabulary.translation: 这款手表是限量版，仅生产了500块。

vocabulary.entry: **appeal to** /əˈpiːl tu/ phr. 吸引，有吸引力
vocabulary.example: This music doesn't really appeal to me.
vocabulary.translation: 这音乐对我没什么吸引力。

vocabulary.example: It is rare to see such a beautiful sunset.
vocabulary.translation: 很难得看到这么美的日落。

vocabulary.entry: **functional** /ˈfʌŋkʃənl/ adj. 功能的，实用的（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The furniture is simple and functional, but not very stylish.
vocabulary.translation: 家具简单实用，但不太时髦。

vocabulary.example: The painting was sold at a famous auction house in London.
vocabulary.translation: 这幅画在伦敦一家著名拍卖行售出。

vocabulary.example: Buying property is often seen as a good long-term investment.

vocabulary.entry: **business opportunity** /ˈbɪznəs ˌɒpəˈtjuːnəti/ n. 商业机会
vocabulary.example: They saw the growing demand for organic food as a great business opportunity.
vocabulary.translation: 他们将有机食品日益增长的需求视为一个绝佳的商机。

vocabulary.entry: **team up with** /ˌtiːm ˈʌp wɪð/ phr. v. 与……合作
vocabulary.example: The company has teamed up with a local charity to raise money.
vocabulary.translation: 这家公司与当地一家慈善机构合作筹集资金。

vocabulary.entry: **feeds into** /ˈfiːdz ˈɪntuː/ phr. v. 促进，助长
vocabulary.example: This new evidence feeds into the existing theory.
vocabulary.translation: 这个新证据支持了现有的理论。

vocabulary.entry: **resale market** /ˈriːseɪl ˈmɑːkɪt/ n. 转售市场
vocabulary.example: There is a huge resale market for concert tickets.
vocabulary.translation: 演唱会门票有一个巨大的转售市场。

vocabulary.entry: **camp out** /ˌkæmp ˈaʊt/ phr. v. 露营；（为购物等）在外面排队等候（口语）
vocabulary.example: Fans started camping out days before the tickets went on sale.
vocabulary.translation: 粉丝们在门票开始发售前几天就开始在外面排队等候。

vocabulary.entry: **get one's hands on** /ˌɡet wʌnz ˈhændz ɒn/ phr. 得到，获得（口语）
vocabulary.example: I'd love to get my hands on a copy of that book.
vocabulary.translation: 我很想得到那本书的副本。

vocabulary.entry: **desirable** /dɪˈzaɪərəbl/ adj. 令人向往的，合意的（书面语）
vocabulary.example: This area of the city is a very desirable place to live.
vocabulary.translation: 城市的这个地区是一个非常理想的居住地。

vocabulary.entry: **flip** /flɪp/ v. 快速转售（以获利）（口语）
vocabulary.example: He bought the old house, renovated it, and flipped it for a profit.
vocabulary.translation: 他买了那栋老房子，翻新后转手赚了一笔。

vocabulary.example: The company made a healthy profit this year.
vocabulary.translation: 公司今年获得了可观的利润。
